case.title: The lead technician dialog offers no Unassigned and assigns on one click
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682423 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682423 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A}, with no shift booked for it on the Schedule. {Technician-B} is not the technician on any of its lines.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682423 One Click and {Work-order-1} is S2-37411.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Open the "More actions" (…) menu on the card for {Work-order-1} in {Technician-A}'s column.
  2. Click "Reassign lead technician".
  3. Read the dialog's list from the top.
  4. Read the dialog's buttons.
  5. Click {Technician-A} in the list.
  6. Open the "More actions" (…) menu on the card for {Work-order-1} again.
  7. Click "Reassign lead technician".
  8. Click {Technician-B} in the list.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu offers "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 2: the "Reassign lead technician" dialog opens.
  • Step 3: a "Search technicians" box, then one list of technicians at {Location-A} with no grouping, each with an avatar and an "N open" count. {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are in it. There is no "Unassigned" row.
  • Step 4: the only button is "Cancel". There is no "Reassign" or other confirm button.
  • Step 5: the dialog closes and nothing changes: {Work-order-1} stays in {Technician-A}'s column and no message shows.
  • Step 6: the menu offers "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 7: the "Reassign lead technician" dialog opens.
  • Step 8: the dialog closes at once, with no other click, and {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column. The message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with an "Undo" button.

Known problem (SV-11522 and SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the dialog lists "Unassigned" at the top, and choosing a technician needs a click on a "Reassign" button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R12: “The dialog offers eligible active technicians in the current location and nothing else. Unassigned is not offered there: Unassigned is the place for work orders without a lead, not a technician, and removing the lead is the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or a drag to Unassigned. It follows the design: a Search technicians box, each technician with their avatar and N open count, no grouping.”
  • S4-R13: “Clicking a technician in the dialog assigns them at once; there is no confirm button, and the dialog’s only button is Cancel. When the shift-clearing prompt applies (S4-R28) it shows first, and the change is made from the prompt. Clicking the work order’s current lead closes the dialog with no change (S4-N4).”
  • S4-N4: “Selecting the current lead again leaves all assignments unchanged and produces no reassignment toast.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • PRD change log, 19 Oct 2026: “S4-R12, S4-R13, S4-R30: Unassigned is no longer offered in the dialog (Unassign stays in the menu, S11-R9); clicking a technician assigns at once, no Reassign button; clicking the current lead closes with no change. v66.”

Not yet checked against a build.

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11524)
